chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to fast in Sha'ban and Ramadan, linking them, and he forbade the people from linking them, and he used to say: 'These two are the months of Allah, and they are an expiation for what is before them and for what is after them from sins.'

key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, known for fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.يَصِلُهُمَا: Linking them (connecting the fasts of Sha'ban directly to the fasts of Ramadan without a break)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of fasting in Sha'ban and linking it to Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s unique practice of fasting throughout Sha'ban and connecting it to Ramadan, while distinguishing his personal devotion from the general community's practice. It highlights the theological significance of these months as divine expiations for sins, reinforcing the concept of continuous spiritual purification in Shia tradition. The emphasis on 'months of Allah' elevates Sha'ban from a mere preparatory period to a sacred time of atonement.
